reason: A has a clear left-to-right order: logo and product, then headline, badges, CTA and legal. Its flaws are that the SUNSET SALE ribbon is jammed against the logo wordmark, the body copy is too small to read, the badge pills are tiny, and the legal block on the right is as heavy as the CTA. B is broken: the headline runs five lines and fills the left third, the CTA sits before the logo, the logo, product and badges are shrunk to specks and scattered, the body and legal text are microscopic single lines, the ribbon collides with the badges, and a missing-image placeholder is visible at the right edge.

A squeezes the body copy into a narrow five-line ragged column, which reads badly. Its NEW FLAVOR badge is as large as the CTA, so the two compete for attention, and 'the Light' sits on a translucent circle. B's right column runs cleanly from headline to copy to CTA, but the big background circle is stretched into an ellipse, 'hour.' is orphaned on its own line, the logo is small and crowded under an oversized badge, and the can overlaps the edge of the ellipse.

A is a reasonable left-to-right banner: brand and badge on the left, the can in the middle, and headline, subline and CTA stacked on the right. Its flaws: the CTA is oversized and sits about 12px from the right edge, the badge nearly touches the left edge, and the logo is moved below the badge and shrunk inside the circle. B breaks the subline into a five-line column ('golden / hour.') stranded between the can and the CTA, out of reading order. B also splits the headline over two lines, leaves a wide gap between the badge and the logo, and the logo wordmark renders as 'SOLST CE', which damages the brand.

A lays the elements out left to right, but the subcopy is squeezed into a tiny five-line column ending in the orphan 'hour.', sits on a translucent circle and can't be read. The logo is microscopic, and the NEW FLAVOR badge is as heavy as the CTA. B groups the headline and subcopy properly and its CTA is strong, but the left cluster is broken: the badge is jammed against the top edge, the SOLSTICE logo is clipped at the bottom and overlaps the circle, and a stray circle fragment sits in the corner. That is real brand damage, but B's message and CTA hierarchy hold up better than A's.

A reads left to right as a banner should: brand, then headline and subcopy, then CTA, with the headline kept on one line. However, the NEW FLAVOR badge is oversized and competes with the CTA, the SOLSTICE logo is tiny and low-contrast on the grey circle, the can is cramped, and 'golden hour.' wraps onto a weak second line. In B, 'Chase / the Light' is split across two lines and loses its punch, the subcopy is jammed against the top edge, and the logo wordmark is almost unreadable. B also fragments the copy, with the headline in the middle and the subcopy stacked over the CTA at the right, so the reading order breaks up.

A: the NEW FLAVOR badge has shrunk until it can't be read. The body copy is squeezed into a narrow 5-line column ('Botanical / sparkling / infusions…') and sits as a stray fragment beside the CTA. The two-line headline runs into the background circle, and the SOLSTICE logo is tiny and cut off from the rest of the brand area, so the layout reads as scattered pieces. B: reads cleanly from left to right. The headline is on one line, with the subcopy and CTA grouped under it on a shared centre axis. Its flaws are that the badge is bigger than the logo and crowds it inside the faded circle, the large left circle makes the composition lopsided, and the can's label text is too small to read.

A: the body copy is squeezed into a narrow column at the far right and wraps onto about six lines of illegible micro-text. The NEW FLAVOR badge and SOLSTICE logo are tiny and crowded together above the headline, the product can is gone, and the oversized CTA crowds out the headline. B reads left to right as a banner should: can, then headline with two-line subcopy, then CTA. However, the can is a tiny unreadable smudge with what looks like the badge colliding with it at top-left, the standalone SOLSTICE logo is missing, and the subcopy is very small at 50px height.

A keeps the original's centred logo, headline and CTA stack with even spacing and a clear hierarchy; its only flaws are a bokeh dot sitting next to 'Summer' in the CTA and a slightly tight stack against the empty side areas. B breaks 'Chase / the Light' onto two lines in a wide banner, so the headline is oversized and jammed against the top edge, and the CTA almost touches the bottom. The small SOLSTICE logo floats on its own at the left without lining up with anything, which leaves a lopsided layout with dead space.

A: the CTA 'Shop the Summer Line' is pushed to the far right edge and wraps awkwardly onto two lines, and a bokeh dot sits on 'Line'. The headline is off-centre, which leaves the left third empty, and the logo above it is tiny and doesn't line up with anything, so the layout looks arbitrary. B: it keeps the original centred stack of logo, headline and CTA, with the headline as the clear focal point and the CTA on one line. Its weaknesses are a vertically cramped stack, a very small logo and wordmark, and a CTA sitting close to the bottom edge, while the left and right sides of the banner are left empty.

A keeps the original one-line headline, the stack is centred and there's room around it. However, the SOLSTICE logo has shrunk to an unreadable size, the sun's rays are gone, and the CTA is scaled up so far that it competes with the headline. B breaks the headline over two oversized lines and pushes the CTA almost to the bottom edge, where it spans nearly the full width. That leaves the bottom cramped next to the empty area at the top. B's logo is also tiny and has lost its rays.

A keeps the original's centred stack (logo, headline, CTA) on one axis, with sensible scale and spacing for the landscape canvas. Its only flaws are minor: a bokeh dot grazes the headline's descender area, and the group sits slightly low with the top band empty. B has no shared alignment edge: the logo is centred around x≈255, the headline starts at x≈55 and the CTA at x≈100. That leaves the right half dead, a large gap between the headline and the CTA, and a bokeh dot colliding with the end of 'Line'.

A: the headline is a cramped 5-line block jammed against the left edge, and the CTA comes before the brand. On the right, the logo, a tiny product, unreadable body copy, the badges and the SUNSET SALE tag are crammed together and collide, and the legal text and placeholder image are illegible. B has a clear left-to-right order (logo/product → headline → badges → CTA) with the headline dominant, but the SUNSET SALE tag overlaps the product, the body copy and badges are tiny, and the legal text is squeezed into a narrow, badly wrapped column against the right edge.

A has a clear left-to-right banner flow (brand/product, then headline, copy, CTA), but the subcopy wraps to leave 'hour.' orphaned on its own line, and the 'NEW FLAVOR' badge is oversized and competes with the tiny SOLSTICE logo stacked under it. The CTA is also a bit heavy. B squeezes the subcopy into a narrow five-line column jammed between the can and the CTA, which is awkward and ragged. Its huge badge competes with the headline, and the headline crowds the decorative circle at the top-right edge.

A: the subcopy is squeezed into a narrow column with ragged wraps ('golden / hour.'), stuck between the can and the CTA, which jumbles the reading order. The SOLSTICE wordmark renders as 'SOLST CE', so the logo is broken, and it's tiny and floating in the circle. B: the headline, subcopy and CTA form a clean right-hand stack in the right order with an intact logo. Flaws in B: the NEW FLAVOR pill is jammed against the left edge, the CTA nearly touches the right edge, and the logo sits awkwardly under the badge instead of in a brand position.

A: the NEW FLAVOR pill sits on top of the SOLSTICE logo. The sun mark is half covered and the wordmark is tiny and faint inside the decorative circle, so the brand is effectively lost and the left end is a jumbled cluster. The headline, subcopy and CTA are well arranged. B: the badge, logo, can, headline and CTA read cleanly from left to right with the logo intact, but the subcopy is crammed into a narrow five-line column of tiny text with one-word lines like 'hour.', which is close to illegible. There is also uneven spacing between the can and the headline.

A: the SOLSTICE logo is shrunk to an illegible speck under an oversized NEW FLAVOR badge. The headline is stacked into two lines and gets cramped, and the subhead is jammed against the top edge over a bubble, so the right half feels crowded. B: the one-line headline with the subhead grouped under it is closer to the original's hierarchy, but the logo is also tiny, the subhead breaks awkwardly ('crafted for / golden hour.'), and the CTA is so big it competes with the headline.

A reads clearly left to right in three zones (brand, can, then headline, subcopy and CTA in a centred stack) with good hierarchy, but the NEW FLAVOR pill outweighs the small SOLSTICE logo stacked under it inside the big circle, and the can sits tight against that cluster with uneven gaps. B is broken: the headline is forced onto two lines and partly sits on the background circle, the subcopy is squeezed into a 5-line ragged column of tiny text, the NEW FLAVOR badge is unreadably small, the logo hangs below its circle, and the CTA is jammed against the right edge.

A reads cleanly from left to right (small can, then the headline with a two-line subline, then a dominant CTA), but it drops the SOLSTICE wordmark and the NEW FLAVOR badge, and the subline is tiny. B keeps the badge and logo but squeezes the logo into a cramped spot between the badge and the headline, drops the can, and wraps the subcopy into an unreadable five-line sliver jammed against the right edge, which makes the cluster look cluttered and the brand lockup illegible.

A breaks the headline into a two-line block that crowds the canvas, nearly touching the top edge with the CTA jammed close beneath it and the bottom edge. The small SOLSTICE logo is stranded alone in a large empty left zone, so the left and right halves feel unrelated and the layout is lopsided. B keeps the original's centred logo, headline and CTA stack with sensible size steps and even margins, making it clearly the same design. Its only flaws are minor: the stack is a little tight vertically and bokeh dots sit close to the headline and CTA.

A keeps the original's centred stack of logo, headline and CTA, with clear hierarchy and faithful colours. Its flaws are minor: a stacked column is a weak use of a wide banner, the logo/wordmark is small, and the CTA sits fairly close to the bottom edge. B pushes the CTA to the far right and wraps it awkwardly onto two lines ('Shop the / Summer Line'). A bokeh dot sits behind 'Summer Line', the headline is off-centre, and the left third is dead space. The SOLSTICE wordmark is shrunk to near-illegible size, so the layout looks lopsided and unintentional.

A: the two-line headline is so big that it pushes 'Shop the Summer Line' into the bottom edge (about 10px margin), and the CTA nearly spans the full width. The SOLSTICE wordmark is a tiny afterthought and the sun icon has lost its rays, so the layout feels jammed rather than airy like the original. B keeps the original's centred, roomy composition with a one-line headline over the CTA and even margins. However, the SOLSTICE wordmark is shrunk to near-illegible micro text, the sun logo is reduced to a dot, and the headline–CTA gap is tighter than in the original.

A shifts everything left but nothing shares an edge: the logo sits around x≈255, the headline starts at x≈55 and the CTA at x≈100. That gives three ragged starting points, with dead space on the right and a big empty gap between headline and CTA. A bokeh dot also hits the 'Line' end of the CTA. B keeps the original's centred axis and stacks logo, headline and CTA in one tight, readable group with clear hierarchy. Its only flaws are a faint bokeh dot just behind the 'Light' descender and a group that sits a little high, leaving loose space at the bottom.

A reads left to right with a clear headline, a stacked badge column and a prominent CTA. However, the SUNSET SALE ribbon collides with the logo and the can, the can is tiny, the legal copy is cramped and illegible in the top-right corner, and a stray grey placeholder chip sits under the CTA. B has the wrong hierarchy: the legal copy is blown up into a large block under the logo and competes with the headline, while the SUNSET SALE badge shrinks to an unreadable chip. The three badges are scattered as tiny fragments (one above the CTA, two below it), and a stray red mark floats beside the headline.

A: the SUNSET SALE ribbon collides with the SOLSTICE logo and the start of the headline. The legal text sits between the headline and the body copy, which breaks the reading order. The product can is gone. The CTA is small and crammed in with the badges, and a clipped image placeholder at the bottom right collides with them. B: the two-column banner keeps the headline and a prominent CTA and gives a clear hierarchy, but the can is tiny and nearly touches the sale ribbon. The body and legal text are close to illegible at this size, and the left column has awkward empty gaps.

A keeps the original's order and the product is large and strong. However, the SOLSTICE logo has drifted right of the centre axis and sits alone, the subtitle wraps so 'golden hour.' hangs on a short second line, and the copy and CTA are crowded at the bottom while the top half is mostly bokeh. B puts the headline over the big translucent circle, and the subtitle runs almost edge to edge with very thin margins. The product shrinks into a small can floating in empty space, the CTA is cut off from its copy by a big gap, and the logo is again off-centre next to the badge, so the layout feels scattered rather than deliberately arranged.

A keeps a sensible top-to-bottom order (badge, logo, can, headline, copy, CTA), but the background circle is stretched into a tall oval, the NEW FLAVOR badge sits awkwardly above the logo and is almost as wide as the column, and the bottom ~90px is dead space below the CTA. B puts the logo and headline first, but it moves the NEW FLAVOR badge to the bottom as a big orange pill stacked over the CTA, so it reads as a second, competing button. That buries the real CTA and separates the badge from the product, and the can floats low inside the same distorted oval.

A gets the hierarchy wrong. The legal disclaimer is set as a large four-line block on the left, as prominent as the body copy. The SUNSET SALE ribbon has shrunk to an unreadable sliver next to the can. The three badges are now microscopic labels around the CTA, and a stray orange dash floats beside the headline. B keeps the SUNSET SALE badge readable and stacks the three badges as a legible column next to the CTA, with the legal text correctly shrunk to fine print. B still has problems: the can is tiny, the badge crowds the logo and product, a stray red fragment sits under the CTA, and the headline is cramped against the badge column.

A uses a sensible two-column banner layout with the headline dominant and the CTA bottom-right. Its flaws: the product can is shrunk to a tiny afterthought, the SUNSET SALE badge floats between the logo and the can, the legal text block is wedged into the left column, and the right column is cramped against the edges. B has worse problems. The SUNSET SALE badge collides with the headline's first line. The legal fine print sits right under the headline, above the body copy, so it ranks too high and breaks the reading order. The product can is gone entirely. A broken placeholder image overlaps the bottom-right corner. The badges and the CTA are jumbled together in a cramped bottom cluster.

A changes the original's order by putting the headline and subcopy at the top. The headline sits over the large translucent circle, and the subcopy runs almost to both side edges. The can is shrunk, with big uneven dead gaps above and below it, and the SOLSTICE logo is pushed off-centre to the right, crowding the circle edge. B keeps the original logo → can → headline → CTA order with a well-sized can. However, its logo is also off-centre to the right, the subcopy wraps into an awkward two-word 'golden hour.' line, and the subcopy and CTA are jammed together at the bottom with little margin.

A: the headline-first stack reads well, but the NEW FLAVOR badge has been moved below the product. It is now a big pill stacked right above the CTA, so it looks like a second button and competes with it. The CTA is almost full-width and jammed against the side edges and the bottom. B: it keeps the original's order (badge, logo, product, headline, copy, CTA), but the badge is almost as big as the CTA and almost full-width, the stretched oval behind the top looks distorted, the subcopy runs nearly edge to edge, and about 100px at the bottom is dead space. B is slightly less confusing because its badge doesn't pose as a second button.
